title: Prototype: Classification Question Type
description: A small interaction test for reusable classification questions. This is not a finished classroom assignment.
directions: Test each classification by dragging, selecting and clicking, and using the keyboard. Correct any highlighted mistakes after the first check. One multiple-choice question is included to verify that question types can be mixed.
submissionInstruction: This is a prototype. Do not submit its test results to the live Google Form.

questions.prompt: Sort each clause by whether it expresses a complete thought.

items.text: Because the stage lights flickered twice
Our class finished the novel yesterday
Although our class finished the novel yesterday
The buses wait beside the gym

questions.explanation: Independent clauses can stand alone as complete thoughts. Dependent clauses begin with words such as because, although, or when and need an independent clause to complete their meaning.

questions.prompt: Sort each sentence by its clause structure.

items.text: The audience applauded the final scene.
The audience applauded, and the actors bowed.
When the final scene ended, the audience applauded.
Maya revised her paragraph and checked every citation.
Maya revised her paragraph, but she missed one citation.
Although Maya revised her paragraph, she missed one citation.

questions.explanation: A simple sentence has one independent clause, a compound sentence has two or more independent clauses, and a complex sentence combines an independent clause with at least one dependent clause.

questions.prompt: Although the rain stopped, the field remained muddy.
questions.explanation: The sentence is complex because it combines the dependent clause “Although the rain stopped” with the independent clause “the field remained muddy.”
